The complete title transition work is folded into the active scene. It uses the real title singleton, four native pointer-to-member states, three held children, original card/direct-input/attract logic and the same cleanup, startup movie, language archive, camera and load/release calls. The native destructor lowers to the original destructor entry for the former explicit destroy body. Asset graphics, audio, particle and technique helpers are inherited from each validated base.

Both authored title-state blocks are represented. The getter reads the same lobby game-mode word, and the actual title actor now owns the checked offline transition, original fade child allocation and bit 2/4 flow.
The active shared declaration now takes the original native title-task receiver. The folded source retains its helper, virtual task and scene initializer contracts.

The predicate checks state 2 on the actual controller and returns its original 0/1 register word. Cursor and destructor declarations are kept on the native owner, supplying the complete original callable interface.

The title readiness predicate and record provider now use actual scene or controller receivers. This accounts for that connection, leaving other historical trial-agreement input, prompt and rendering changes outside the replay.

Private source owns the paired four load/release stages and the four 12-byte pointer-to-member records, archive filenames, title music and particle position, all verified at original linked data offsets.
